A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Wavelet Diffusion Neural Operator and contain the complete 43-page paper, including Appendices A–L. Corresponding text, equations, figures, tables, and algorithms support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulation, control, super-resolution, ablation, and robustness results in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical studies and reports revised numerical outcomes in several main-text and appendix tables.

M1.justification: Wavelet-domain diffusion, control guidance, and the base-resolution/super-resolution training and inference procedures remain unchanged. Section 3, Algorithm 1, and the model descriptions in Appendices F–H retain the same method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Burgers’, advection, compressible Navier–Stokes, incompressible-fluid, and ERA5 tasks, with the same control and super-resolution scenarios. Adding advection and ERA5 to the conclusion reflects experiments already present in v1.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same baseline membership. In particular, Table 5 already includes Transolver, CNO, MSVI, ACDM, and DiffusionPDE in v1. Revised FNO scores do not establish a changed comparison method.

E3.justification: Reported splits, sample sizes, metrics, resolutions, and training/inference settings are unchanged. The introduction corrects '3,8854' control variables to 3,584, matching the setting already stated in Section 4.4 of v1.

E4.justification: Appendix C.3 revises the numerical evidence testing approximate scale invariance through mixed-resolution versus individual-resolution FNO training. Mixed training previously won at all three resolutions; revised Table 6 gives it a slight disadvantage at twice-downsampled resolution. Other ablation, sensitivity, and robustness studies remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same mean and standard deviation reporting over 50 test samples in Appendix C.5 and Table 10. No seed information, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or statistical tests are added or revised.

E6.justification: Under unchanged reported settings, Table 2b changes WDNO's smoke-control objective from 0.2047 to 0.0679, while BPPO remains 0.3066. Table 1 changes FNO's Burgers’ MSE from 0.01091 to 0.00015 and its 2D-fluid MSE from 0.00403 to 0.00684. Table 6 and FNO results in Tables 16–17/Figure 4 also change. These revisions substantially alter performance margins; Table 17 now gives FNO a narrow advantage over WDNO at zero upsampling with nearest interpolation.

T1.justification: The PDE definitions, wavelet decomposition, scale-transformation reasoning, objectives, and mathematical material in Appendix A are unchanged. No theorem, proof, or substantive derivation is added or revised.

C1.justification: The two methodological contributions and application scope remain intact, but the highlighted smoke-leakage reduction increases from 33.2% to 78% in the abstract and 79% in the introduction. Table 2b supports approximately 77.9%, so the two revised headline percentages are not fully consistent.

C2.justification: Mechanism explanations, applicability claims, and Section 5 limitations remain unchanged. The interpretations concerning diffusion-model superiority and mixed-resolution training are retained despite the revised evidence; changed numerical observations are assessed under E6.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware, timings, and data-generation instructions are unchanged. The repository URL added to the abstract identifies the same repository already linked in Section 4 of v1, so it does not establish newly available resources.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive positioning in Appendix D remain unchanged. The added ICLR publication header is a publication-status edit, not a revision of the relationship to prior research.

P1.justification: Limited abstract, introduction, and conclusion edits add a visible code URL, correct the control-variable typo, update performance wording, and list existing benchmarks more completely. Section organization and appendix structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds the conference-publication header and slightly reflows the first page. Figure 4's FNO curves reflect revised results, while its axes and legends remain the same. Figure/table membership, placement, and overall layout are retained.

improvement.justification: The corrected control-variable count and more visible code link improve clarity, but the PDFs do not explain the substantial score revisions or establish whether they correct earlier reporting. Some retained wording is less well supported: Section 4.1 still says diffusion models 'far surpass' other baselines despite FNO now nearly matching them, and Appendix C.3 leaves its mixed-training superiority statement unqualified despite Table 6's exception. These effects do not establish a reliable net quality improvement or decline.
